claim: Buruli ulcer (BU) is a neglected tropical disease caused by infection of subcutaneous tissue with Mycobacterium ulcerans.
source: Buruli ulcer (BU) is a neglected tropical disease caused by infection of subcutaneous tissue with Mycobacterium ulcerans.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about BU that draws from established scientific knowledge and is supported by the broader scientific literature.

claim: BU is commonly reported across rural regions of Central and West Africa.
source: BU is commonly reported across rural regions of Central and West Africa but has been increasing dramatically in temperate southeast Australia around the major metropolitan city of Melbourne, with most disease transmission occurring in the summer months.
evidence: This statement reflects established epidemiological knowledge about the geographic distribution of BU.

claim: BU has been increasing dramatically in temperate southeast Australia around the major metropolitan city of Melbourne.
source: BU is commonly reported across rural regions of Central and West Africa but has been increasing dramatically in temperate southeast Australia around the major metropolitan city of Melbourne, with most disease transmission occurring in the summer months.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data presented in the study and references to the increasing case numbers in Victoria.

claim: Most BU disease transmission in southeast Australia occurs in the summer months.
source: BU is commonly reported across rural regions of Central and West Africa but has been increasing dramatically in temperate southeast Australia around the major metropolitan city of Melbourne, with most disease transmission occurring in the summer months.
evidence: This is supported by cited research on seasonal transmission patterns.

claim: Australian native possums are reservoirs of M. ulcerans.
source: Previous research has shown that Australian native possums are reservoirs of M. ulcerans and that they shed the bacteria in their fecal material (excreta).
evidence: This claim is supported by previous research findings cited in the manuscript.

claim: Australian native possums shed M. ulcerans bacteria in their fecal material (excreta).
source: Previous research has shown that Australian native possums are reservoirs of M. ulcerans and that they shed the bacteria in their fecal material (excreta).
evidence: This is supported by previous research and the data collected in this study.

claim: Locales where possums harbor M. ulcerans overlap with human cases of BU.
source: Field surveys show that locales where possums harbor M. ulcerans overlap with human cases of BU, raising the possibility of using possum excreta surveys to predict the risk of disease occurrence in humans.
evidence: This is supported by field survey data and spatial analysis presented in the study.

claim: A 12-month possum excreta surveillance program was established across an area of 350 km2 in the Mornington Peninsula area 70 km south of Melbourne, Australia.
source: We thus established a highly structured 12 month possum excreta surveillance program across an area of 350 km2 in the Mornington Peninsula area 70 km south of Melbourne, Australia.
evidence: This describes the methodology of the study as implemented by the researchers.

claim: Over two sampling campaigns in summer and winter, 2,282 possum excreta specimens were collected.
source: Over two sampling campaigns in summer and winter, we collected 2,282 possum excreta specimens of which 11% were PCR positive for M. ulcerans-specific DNA.
evidence: This is a direct report of the data collected during the study.

claim: 11% of collected possum excreta specimens were PCR positive for M. ulcerans-specific DNA.
source: Over two sampling campaigns in summer and winter, we collected 2,282 possum excreta specimens of which 11% were PCR positive for M. ulcerans-specific DNA.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the PCR testing performed in the study.

claim: Non-random, co-correlated clustering of both M. ulcerans positive possum excreta and human BU cases was observed using SaTScan.
source: Using the spatial scanning statistical tool SaTScan, we observed non-random, co-correlated clustering of both M. ulcerans positive possum excreta and human BU cases.
evidence: This is a result from the spatial statistical analysis performed in the study.

claim: The excreta model performance was superior to a null model trained using the previous year's human BU case incidence data (AUC 0.66 vs 0.55) for the Mornington Peninsula.
source: By observing where human BU cases subsequently occurred, we show that the excreta model performance was superior to a null model trained using the previous year's human BU case incidence data (AUC 0.66 vs 0.55).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of model performance based on the study's statistical analysis.

claim: A new survey of 661 possum excreta specimens was conducted in Geelong, a geographically separate BU endemic area to the southwest of Melbourne.
source: We then used data unseen by the excreta-informed model from a new survey of 661 possum excreta specimens in Geelong, a geographically separate BU endemic area to the southwest of Melbourne, to prospectively predict the location of human BU cases in that region.
evidence: This describes the validation dataset collected in a separate geographic area.

claim: For Geelong, the excreta-based BU prediction model outperformed the null model (AUC 0.75 vs 0.50).
source: As for the Mornington Peninsula, the excreta-based BU prediction model outperformed the null model (AUC 0.75 vs 0.50) and pinpointed specific locations in Geelong where interventions could be deployed to interrupt disease spread.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the prospective validation of the model in a new geographic area.

claim: The excreta-based model pinpointed specific locations in Geelong where interventions could be deployed to interrupt disease spread.
source: As for the Mornington Peninsula, the excreta-based BU prediction model outperformed the null model (AUC 0.75 vs 0.50) and pinpointed specific locations in Geelong where interventions could be deployed to interrupt disease spread.
evidence: This is an inference based on the model's ability to identify high-risk areas.

claim: There is a quantitative relationship between possum excreta shedding of M. ulcerans and humans developing BU.
source: This study highlights the One Health nature of BU by confirming a quantitative relationship between possum excreta shedding of M. ulcerans and humans developing BU.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the statistical modeling and spatial correlation analysis.

claim: BU is an infection of subcutaneous tissues that can leave patients with disability and life-long deformity.
source: BU is an infection of subcutaneous tissues that can leave patients with disability and life-long deformity.
evidence: This is established medical knowledge about the clinical consequences of BU.

claim: Mycobacterium ulcerans is a slow-growing environmental bacterium that can infect humans after introduction through skin micro-trauma.
source: The causative agent, Mycobacterium ulcerans is a slow-growing environmental bacterium that can infect humans after introduction through skin micro-trauma (Portaels et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by cited research on the characteristics and transmission of M. ulcerans.

claim: The exact environmental reservoir(s) and mode(s) of transmission of BU are unresolved.
source: While the exact environmental reservoir(s) and mode(s) of transmission of BU are unresolved, they do continue to be the subject of intense research.
evidence: This acknowledges the current state of scientific knowledge about BU transmission.

claim: BU has a highly focal geographical distribution and typically occurs around low-lying marshlands and riverine areas.
source: The disease has a highly focal geographical distribution and typically occurs around low-lying marshlands and riverine areas.
evidence: This is established epidemiological knowledge about BU distribution patterns.

claim: BU occurs mostly in tropical and subtropical areas of West and Central Africa.
source: BU occurs mostly in tropical and subtropical areas of West and Central Africa however smaller foci are recognized in South America, Southeast Asia, and Australasia (Röltgen and Pluschke, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited epidemiological literature.

claim: Smaller BU foci are recognized in South America, Southeast Asia, and Australasia.
source: BU occurs mostly in tropical and subtropical areas of West and Central Africa however smaller foci are recognized in South America, Southeast Asia, and Australasia (Röltgen and Pluschke, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited epidemiological literature.

claim: In Australia, small disease foci have been described in coastal regions of Queensland and the Northern Territory.
source: In Australia, although small disease foci have been described in coastal regions of Queensland and the Northern Territory, the majority of the disease burden is found in the temperate state of Victoria, where several outbreaks have been recorded over the past three decades (Johnson, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on Australian BU epidemiology.

claim: The majority of the BU disease burden in Australia is found in the temperate state of Victoria.
source: In Australia, although small disease foci have been described in coastal regions of Queensland and the Northern Territory, the majority of the disease burden is found in the temperate state of Victoria, where several outbreaks have been recorded over the past three decades (Johnson, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature and the data presented in the study.

claim: Several BU outbreaks have been recorded in Victoria over the past three decades.
source: In Australia, although small disease foci have been described in coastal regions of Queensland and the Northern Territory, the majority of the disease burden is found in the temperate state of Victoria, where several outbreaks have been recorded over the past three decades (Johnson, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on Victorian BU history.

claim: In Victoria, the median incubation period for BU is 4.8 months.
source: In Victoria, it has been established that the median incubation period is 4.8 months with peak M. ulcerans transmission in humans occurring in late summer (Loftus et al., 2018; Trubiano et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by cited epidemiological studies.

claim: Peak M. ulcerans transmission in humans in Victoria occurs in late summer.
source: In Victoria, it has been established that the median incubation period is 4.8 months with peak M. ulcerans transmission in humans occurring in late summer (Loftus et al., 2018; Trubiano et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by cited epidemiological studies.

claim: Several cases of BU infections have been reported in native wildlife and domestic mammal species including common ringtail, common brushtail, and mountain brushtail possums.
source: Several cases of BU infections have also been reported in native wildlife and domestic mammal species including common ringtail (Pseudocheirus peregrinus), common brushtail (Trichosurus vulpecula), mountain brushtail possums (Trichosurus cunninghami) (O'Brien et al., 2014; Portaels et al., 2001), koalas (Phascolarctos cinereus) (Portaels et al., 2001), long footed potoroos (Potorous longipes), dogs (O'Brien et al., 2011), cats (Elsner et al., 2008), horses (van Zyl et al., 2010), and alpacas (Portaels et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited case reports and studies.

claim: BU infections have been reported in koalas, long footed potoroos, dogs, cats, horses, and alpacas.
source: Several cases of BU infections have also been reported in native wildlife and domestic mammal species including common ringtail (Pseudocheirus peregrinus), common brushtail (Trichosurus vulpecula), mountain brushtail possums (Trichosurus cunninghami) (O'Brien et al., 2014; Portaels et al., 2001), koalas (Phascolarctos cinereus) (Portaels et al., 2001), long footed potoroos (Potorous longipes), dogs (O'Brien et al., 2011), cats (Elsner et al., 2008), horses (van Zyl et al., 2010), and alpacas (Portaels et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited case reports.

claim: Naturally acquired BU infections in animals have occurred across the same geographical regions of Victoria where BU is known to be endemic for humans.
source: These naturally acquired BU infections in animals have occurred across the same geographical regions of Victoria where BU is known to be endemic for humans.
evidence: This is an observation based on the geographic distribution of reported animal cases.

claim: BU is a zoonosis that first causes epizootic disease in local native possum populations and then spills over to humans.
source: Several studies from Victoria suggest that BU is a zoonosis that first causes epizootic disease in the local native possum populations and then spills over to humans.
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by multiple lines of evidence from cited studies.

claim: Possums excrete M. ulcerans DNA in their feces in regions known to be endemic for humans while similar surveys outside endemic areas yielded negative results.
source: Focused field surveys have revealed that possums excrete M. ulcerans DNA in their feces (excreta) in regions known to be endemic for humans while similar surveys outside endemic areas yielded negative results (Fyfe et al., 2010; Carson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by cited field survey studies.

claim: The highest concentrations of M. ulcerans were found in possum excreta compared to other environmental samples.
source: While M. ulcerans DNA could be detected at low levels in a variety of other environmental samples in these studies, by far the highest concentrations of M. ulcerans were found in possum excreta (Fyfe et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by cited comparative environmental sampling studies.

claim: Subclinical M. ulcerans gut carriage in possums is common.
source: Subsequent capture and clinical assessment of free-ranging possums validated the findings of these excreta surveys by showing that subclinical M. ulcerans gut carriage in possums was common while a number of animals had laboratory-confirmed BU skin lesions and in some cases, advanced systemic disease (O'Brien et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by cited possum capture and clinical assessment studies.

claim: Some possums had laboratory-confirmed BU skin lesions and in some cases, advanced systemic disease.
source: Subsequent capture and clinical assessment of free-ranging possums validated the findings of these excreta surveys by showing that subclinical M. ulcerans gut carriage in possums was common while a number of animals had laboratory-confirmed BU skin lesions and in some cases, advanced systemic disease (O'Brien et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by cited clinical assessment studies of possums.

claim: 65% of IS2404-positive possum excreta were also positive by a 16S rRNA bacterial viability assay.
source: Notwithstanding the technical issues with culturing slow-growing M. ulcerans from complex microbial samples, a recent environmental survey identified 65% of IS2404-positive possum excreta were also positive by a 16S rRNA bacterial viability assay (Blasdell et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from a cited environmental survey study.

claim: M. ulcerans strains isolated from human and possum lesions are part of the same transmission cycles.
source: Finally, whole genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis have shown that M. ulcerans strains isolated from human and possum lesions are part of the same transmission cycles (Fyfe et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by cited genomic analysis studies.

claim: In Australia, BU is a One Health issue, with arboreal marsupial mammals representing an important environmental reservoir for M. ulcerans.
source: These findings suggest that in Australia, BU is a One Health issue, with arboreal marsupial mammals representing an important environmental reservoir for M. ulcerans.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence presented in the manuscript.

claim: The present outbreak on the Mornington Peninsula in Victoria is the largest on record in Australia, with over 2,200 laboratory-confirmed cases diagnosed since 2010.
source: The present outbreak on the Mornington Peninsula in Victoria is the largest on record in Australia, with over 2,200 laboratory-confirmed cases diagnosed since 2010 (Department of Health. Victoria A, 2022a).
evidence: This is supported by cited public health surveillance data.

claim: A significant cluster of BU emerged in 2019 in a suburb of the major regional city of Geelong near the Bellarine Peninsula.
source: Concurrent with the Mornington Peninsula outbreak, has been the emergence in 2019 of a significant cluster of BU in a suburb of the major regional city of Geelong near the Bellarine Peninsula.
evidence: This is based on epidemiological surveillance data.

claim: Regions of the Bellarine Peninsula became a BU focus beginning in the late 1990s.
source: Regions of the Bellarine Peninsula became a BU focus beginning in the late 1990s.
evidence: This is historical epidemiological information.

claim: BU endemic areas in Victoria have expanded to within 5 km of the Melbourne city centre.
source: The unprecedented increase in human BU cases since 2010 and the rapid expansion of BU endemic areas in Victoria, including incursions to within 5 km of the Melbourne city centre (Department of Health. Victoria A, 2022b) have highlighted how new strategies to control transmission are urgently required.
evidence: This is supported by cited public health surveillance data.

claim: The long 5 month incubation period of BU in humans complicates attributing disease acquisition to a particular event or location.
source: However, the use of traditional epidemiological surveillance methods to track the emergence and movement of BU disease foci is severely limited by the long 5 month incubation period of the disease in humans (Loftus et al., 2018; Trubiano et al., 2013), which complicates attributing disease acquisition to a particular event or location.
evidence: This is supported by cited epidemiological studies on BU incubation period.

claim: Wildlife sentinels are increasingly being explored for surveillance of zoonotic pathogens like Borrelia burgdorferi, West Nile virus, and Rabies virus.
source: Surveillance programs for a number of zoonotic pathogens like Borrelia burgdorferi, West Nile virus (Hamer et al., 2012), and Rabies virus (Childs et al., 2007) are increasingly exploring the use of wildlife sentinels to monitor disease emergence and spread.
evidence: This is supported by cited examples of wildlife sentinel surveillance programs.

claim: The Mornington Peninsula is located 70 km south of Melbourne's city center and occupies a 750 km2 area.
source: The Mornington Peninsula is located 70 km south of Melbourne's city center and occupies a 750 km2 area that separates Port Phillip Bay from Western Port Bay.
evidence: This is geographic and factual information about the study site.

claim: The Mornington Peninsula separates Port Phillip Bay from Western Port Bay.
source: The Mornington Peninsula is located 70 km south of Melbourne's city center and occupies a 750 km2 area that separates Port Phillip Bay from Western Port Bay.
evidence: This is geographic information about the study site.

claim: Much of the native vegetation of the Mornington Peninsula was cleared under pressure from urban development.
source: Since then, much of the native vegetation of the peninsula was cleared under pressure from urban development although fragmented pockets of remnant wild habitat have been preserved in the Mornington Peninsula National Park and are located southwest of the peninsula (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is historical and environmental information about the study area.

claim: Fragmented pockets of remnant wild habitat have been preserved in the Mornington Peninsula National Park.
source: Since then, much of the native vegetation of the peninsula was cleared under pressure from urban development although fragmented pockets of remnant wild habitat have been preserved in the Mornington Peninsula National Park and are located southwest of the peninsula (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is environmental information about the study area.

claim: The study site is characterized by calcareous sandy soils that support a dense coastal scrubland.
source: The study site overlaps with the western tip of the Mornington Peninsula and is characterized by calcareous sandy soils that support a dense coastal scrubland.
evidence: This is environmental information about the study site.

claim: A large proportion of the houses in the study region serve as temporary tourist accommodations.
source: As the western tip of the peninsula is primarily a local tourist hotspot known for its affluent coastal resorts, a large proportion of the houses in the region serve as temporary tourist accommodations.
evidence: This is demographic and land use information about the study area.

claim: Many residential properties in the study area are spacious holiday homes set in fenced gardens planted with shrubs and trees, which represent ideal possum habitats.
source: Many of the residential properties in the study area are spacious holiday homes, set in fenced gardens planted with shrubs and trees, which represent ideal possum habitats.
evidence: This is environmental and ecological information about the study area.

claim: Geelong is located approximately 65 km southwest of Melbourne.
source: To the west of the Mornington Peninsula, and on the opposite side of the Port Phillip Bay, lies Geelong at the eastern end of Corio Bay and the left bank of the Barwon River, approximately 65 km southwest of Melbourne.
evidence: This is geographic information about the second study site.

claim: Geelong has an estimated urban population of 201,924 as of June 2018.
source: Geelong has an estimated urban population of 201,924 (as of June 2018) and is the second-largest city in Victoria after Melbourne (Australian Bureau of Statistics, 2019b).
evidence: This is demographic data from cited census statistics.

claim: Geelong is the second-largest city in Victoria after Melbourne.
source: Geelong has an estimated urban population of 201,924 (as of June 2018) and is the second-largest city in Victoria after Melbourne (Australian Bureau of Statistics, 2019b).
evidence: This is demographic information from cited census statistics.

claim: Since 2019, BU has been considered endemic in the Geelong suburb of Belmont and surrounding areas, with local transmission suspected.
source: Since 2019, BU has been considered endemic in the Geelong suburb of Belmont and surrounding areas, with local transmission suspected.
evidence: This is epidemiological information about disease status in the area.

claim: Open Data Kit (ODK) is an open-source suite of tools designed to build data collection platforms.
source: Large-scale electronic data collection was organized using the 'Build,' 'Collect,' and 'Aggregate' tools of 'Open Data Kit (ODK),' an open-source suite of tools that were designed to build data collection platforms (Hartung et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a description of the software tool used, supported by citation.

claim: A sampling spacing interval of 200 m was chosen to prevent re-sampling excreta from the same possum between adjacent points.
source: To prevent re-sampling excreta from the same possum between adjacent points a sampling spacing interval of 200 m was chosen which reflects the typical home range (radius <100 m) of these highly territorial animals (Carson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a methodological decision based on cited knowledge of possum home range.

claim: The typical home range radius of possums is less than 100 m.
source: To prevent re-sampling excreta from the same possum between adjacent points a sampling spacing interval of 200 m was chosen which reflects the typical home range (radius <100 m) of these highly territorial animals (Carson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is ecological information about possums from cited literature.

claim: The search for possum excreta was restricted to a 50 m radius around the sampling point and was terminated if no excreta could be found after 5 minutes.
source: The search was restricted to a 50 m radius around the sampling point and was terminated in case no excreta could be found after a pre-allotted time of 5 min.
evidence: This is a methodological detail of the sampling protocol.

claim: Up to three excreta samples were collected at each sampling location, selecting the freshest most intact excreta when more were available.
source: If possible, up to three excreta samples were sampled and, in case more were available, the freshest most intact excreta were selected.
evidence: This is a methodological detail of the sampling protocol.

claim: The summer survey was conducted from December 19, 2018 to March 14, 2019.
source: Several sampling missions were organized from December 19, 2018 to March 14, 2019 and are hereafter referred to as the 'summer survey.'
evidence: This is a temporal detail of the study design.

claim: The winter survey was conducted between May 28 and September 19, 2019.
source: Later, between May 28 and September 19, 2019, we attempted to revisit most of the locations we sampled during summer, a period that is hereafter referred to as the 'winter survey.'
evidence: This is a temporal detail of the study design.

claim: The Geelong survey was conducted from January 16 through to April 28, 2020.
source: Another survey mission centered on the Geelong area was conducted in the early half of 2020 (January 16 through to the April 28, 2020) using the above mentioned surveying methodology with a 200 m grid.
evidence: This is a temporal detail of the study design.

claim: Real-time PCR assays targeting IS2404 were multiplexed with an internal positive control (IPC).
source: Real-time PCR assays targeting IS2404 multiplexed with an internal positive control (IPC) (Life Technologies Cat# 4308323) were carried out as described before (Fyfe et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a methodological detail of the molecular assay.

claim: A real-time PCR cycle threshold (Ct) value <40 was considered positive for M. ulcerans.
source: A real-time PCR cycle threshold (Ct) value <40 was considered positive for M. ulcerans.
evidence: This is a methodological criterion for interpreting PCR results.

claim: The threshold of Ct <40 for M. ulcerans positivity was based on previous performance evaluations of the assay.
source: This threshold was based on previous performance evaluations of the assay (Wallace et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a methodological justification based on cited validation studies.

claim: All extraction negative controls showed the expected results, indicating no contamination was introduced during DNA extraction.
source: All extraction negative controls showed the expected results, indicating that no contamination was introduced during the DNA extraction process.
evidence: This is a quality control result from the laboratory procedures.

claim: All real-time PCR controls (positive and negative) produced the expected results, indicating the amplification reaction was specific and sensitive.
source: Similarly, all real-time PCR controls (positive and negative controls) produced the expected results, indicating that the amplification reaction was specific and sensitive.
evidence: This is a quality control result from the laboratory procedures.

claim: All internal positive controls (IPCs) were detected in the samples, demonstrating the efficiency of the real-time PCR reaction and the absence of inhibitory substances.
source: Furthermore, all IPCs were detected in the samples, demonstrating the efficiency of the real-time PCR reaction and the absence of inhibitory substances.
evidence: This is a quality control result from the laboratory procedures.

claim: Mesh blocks are relatively homogeneous statistical units and represent the smallest geographical unit for which publicly available census data are tabulated by the Australian Bureau of Statistics.
source: Mesh blocks are relatively homogeneous statistical units and represent the smallest geographical unit for which publicly available census data are tabulated by the ABS.
evidence: This is a definition of the geographic unit used in the analysis.

claim: BU has been a 'notifiable condition' in Victoria since 2004.
source: Note that BU has been a 'notifiable condition' in Victoria since 2004 and as of January 1, 2011 DH has been collecting enhanced BU surveillance data in a centralized notifiable disease database using custom collection forms (Victorian Government, 2022).
evidence: This is public health policy information from cited government sources.

claim: As of January 1, 2011, the Victorian Department of Health has been collecting enhanced BU surveillance data in a centralized notifiable disease database.
source: Note that BU has been a 'notifiable condition' in Victoria since 2004 and as of January 1, 2011 DH has been collecting enhanced BU surveillance data in a centralized notifiable disease database using custom collection forms (Victorian Government, 2022).
evidence: This is public health surveillance information from cited government sources.

claim: Mesh blocks typically encompass between 30 and 60 dwellings.
source: As mesh blocks typically encompass between 30 and 60 dwellings the extract of the notifiable disease database was effectively anonymized.
evidence: This is information about the geographic unit used for data aggregation.

claim: The mean incubation period of BU in Victoria is 143 days (Inter-Quartile Range 101–171).
source: We define the incubation period here as the time between exposure to an endemic region and symptom onset. Patients were suspected of having been infected with M. ulcerans in the Mornington Peninsula if they were either a resident of the peninsula or if they visited the area and had not reported recent (<12 months) contact with any other known BU endemic areas in the state (Figure 2—figure supplement 1). A population of cases whose exposure interval overlapped with the survey of the Geelong region was also selected (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is epidemiological data from cited studies.

claim: There was no significant difference between excreta IS2404 positivity and the sampling season (p=0.2933).
source: However, we observed no significant difference between excreta IS2404 positivity and the sampling season (p=0.2933, Fisher's exact test).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: No difference was found between the proportion of M. ulcerans IS2404-positive excreta specimens and possum species (p=0.1309).
source: Additionally, no difference was found between the proportion of M. ulcerans IS2404-positive excreta specimens and possum species (p=0.1309, Fisher's exact test).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: The Ct values for IS2404 real-time PCR ranged from 25.6 to 40.0, corresponding to an estimated M. ulcerans excreta load of 5–24,000 mycobacterial genomes per fecal pellet.
source: The Ct values for IS2404 real-time PCR ranged from 25.6 to 40.0, corresponding to an estimated M. ulcerans excreta load of 5–24,000 mycobacterial genomes per fecal pellet (Wallace et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the PCR analysis, with load estimates based on cited standard curves.

claim: Sampling season had a small but statistically significant impact on the fecal mycobacterial load (t(308)=-2.4, p=0.0171).
source: Interestingly, we noted that sampling season had a small but statistically significant impact on the fecal mycobacterial load (t(308)=-2.4, p=0.0171).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: M. ulcerans positive excreta analyzed in summer had a Ct(IS2404) that was 0.87 lower than excreta collected in winter, corresponding to a 1.8 times higher mycobacterial load in summer excreta material.
source: On average, M. ulcerans positive excreta analyzed in summer had a Ct(IS2404) that was 0.87 lower than excreta collected in winter, a difference which corresponds with a 1.8 times higher mycobacterial load in summer excreta material.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the comparative analysis of seasonal data.

claim: No statistically significant difference was observed between the fecal mycobacterial loads of the two possum species.
source: We observed no statistically significant difference between the fecal mycobacterial loads of the two possum species (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis, supported by Figure 1.

claim: A total of 2,402 locations were visited during the two sampling seasons.
source: A total of 2,402 locations were visited during the two sampling seasons (summer: November 2018 - February 2019 and winter: May 2019 – August 2019).
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of the sampling effort.

claim: In only 120 of all visited locations (5%) no excreta was found within the allotted 5 min survey time per site.
source: In only 120 of all visited locations (5%) no excreta was found within the allotted 5 min survey time per site.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the field survey.

claim: The residential areas of the Mornington Peninsula support a large possum population.
source: This observation indicates that the residential areas of the Mornington Peninsula support a large possum population.
evidence: This is an inference based on the high frequency of finding possum excreta.

claim: Brushtail possum excreta was less frequent than ringtail excreta.
source: During the surveys, excreta from common ringtail and common brushtail possums (hereafter referred to as ringtail and brushtail possums) were identified. Brushtail possum excreta was less frequent than ringtail excreta.
evidence: This is an observation from the field survey data.

claim: M. ulcerans DNA was detected by IS2404 real-time PCR in 310 of all 2,282 (13.6%) excreta specimens.
source: M. ulcerans DNA was detected by IS2404 real-time PCR in 310 of all 2,282 (13.6%) excreta specimens (Table 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the PCR screening, presented in Table 1.

claim: Across the two sampling seasons, spatial scan statistics revealed three statistically significant geographical areas where IS2404-positive excreta clustered non-randomly.
source: Across the two sampling seasons, spatial scan statistics revealed three statistically significant geographical areas where IS2404-positive excreta clustered non-randomly (Table 2).
evidence: This is a result from the spatial statistical analysis, detailed in Table 2.

claim: The Sorrento SaTScan summer cluster encompassed an area where excreta with the highest M. ulcerans DNA concentrations of this study was identified.
source: Of note, the Sorrento SaTScan summer cluster encompassed an area where excreta with the highest M. ulcerans DNA concentrations of this study was also identified (Figure 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the spatial analysis and molecular data, shown in Figure 2.

claim: The spatial distribution of IS2404-positive possum excreta shifted to some extent between summer and winter sampling.
source: Interestingly, the spatial distribution of IS2404-positive possum excreta shifted to some extent between summer and winter sampling, suggesting possum populations might undergo waves of carriage over time (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the comparative spatial analysis, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Possum populations might undergo waves of M. ulcerans carriage over time.
source: Interestingly, the spatial distribution of IS2404-positive possum excreta shifted to some extent between summer and winter sampling, suggesting possum populations might undergo waves of carriage over time (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed seasonal shift in spatial distribution.

claim: Two populations of BU patients were identified that were highly likely to have been infected in the Mornington Peninsula during the summer (n=62) and winter (n=35) excreta surveys.
source: As a result, two populations of BU patients were identified that were highly likely to have been infected in the Mornington Peninsula during the summer (n=62) and winter (n=35) excreta surveys.
evidence: This is a result from the epidemiological case selection based on exposure intervals.

claim: The Mornington Peninsula's population at risk was 144,817 inhabitants as recorded in the 2011 census.
source: Additionally, the population-at-risk from which BU cases arose was represented by the Mornington Peninsula's 144,817 inhabitants as recorded in the 2011 census.
evidence: This is demographic data from the census used in the analysis.

claim: Spatial scan statistics applied to mesh block data revealed three statistically significant clusters where human BU cases aggregated non-randomly.
source: Spatial scan statistics applied to these mesh block data for these BU cases revealed three statistically significant clusters across the two sampling seasons where human BU cases aggregated non-randomly.
evidence: This is a result from the spatial statistical analysis of human case data.

claim: There was a significant spatial correlation between the three clusters of human BU disease and the three clusters with high occurrence of M. ulcerans positive possum excreta.
source: Across the two sampling seasons, there was a significant spatial correlation between the three clusters of human BU disease and the three clusters with high occurrence of M. ulcerans positive possum excreta (Table 3, Figures 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a result from the comparative spatial analysis, shown in Table 3, Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The frequency of excreta positivity for M. ulcerans observed in this study (13.6% for common ringtail possums) was similar to an earlier, smaller survey from the Mornington Peninsula (9.3%).
source: Of note too, the frequency of excreta positivity for M. ulcerans we observed (13.6% for common ringtail possums) was similar to an earlier, smaller survey from the Mornington Peninsula (9.3%) (Fyfe et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a comparison with cited previous survey data.

claim: The excreta-informed model for the Mornington Peninsula demonstrated superior ability under spatial-block cross-validation with a mean AUC of 0.66 compared to 0.56 for the null model.
source: The statistical model developed to prospectively predict the probability of a mesh block containing a case demonstrated a superior ability under spatial-block cross-validation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) to rank mesh blocks according to whether they contained a case or not during the exposure interval – the Receiver-Operating-Characteristic (ROC) AUC value - with a mean AUC of 0.66. This is compared to a mean AUC of 0.56 for a null model based on the preceding year's human BU case incidence data for the Mornington Peninsula (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the model validation analysis, shown in Figure 4.

claim: Three confirmed human BU cases were reported from the Geelong region with a transmission interval that overlapped the sampling period.
source: Three confirmed human BU cases were reported from the Geelong region with a transmission interval that overlapped the sampling period (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is epidemiological data from the Geelong validation study, shown in Figure 5.

claim: The model applied to Geelong data achieved an AUC of 0.75 compared with a null model AUC of 0.50.
source: The model achieved an AUC of 0.75 (Figure 4C), compared with a null model based on the previous year BU case incidence with an AUC score of 0.50, underscoring the predictive ability of the excreta-informed model (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the prospective model validation, shown in Figure 4.

claim: M. ulcerans DNA was detected by IS2404 real-time PCR in 21 of the 661 (3.2%) excreta specimens collected in Geelong.
source: M. ulcerans DNA was detected by IS2404 real-time PCR in 21 of the 661 (3.2%) excreta specimens (Table 4).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the Geelong survey PCR screening, shown in Table 4.

claim: In Geelong, the proportion of IS2404-positive excreta was not significantly different between ringtail and brushtail possums (p=1).
source: As observed with the Mornington Peninsula survey, Ringtail possum excreta was more frequently found than Brushtail possum excreta but the proportion IS2404-positive was not significantly different (p=1, Fisher's exact test) (Table 4).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the Geelong data analysis, shown in Table 4.

claim: The excreta-informed models demonstrated a greater ability to classify case-containing mesh blocks into the top 5%, 10%, 20%, and 50% of top-ranking mesh blocks than the null models.
source: The excreta-informed models deployed in both the Mornington Peninsula and Geelong areas demonstrated a greater ability to classify case-containing mesh blocks into the 5%, 10%, 20%, and 50% of top-ranking mesh blocks than that of the null models (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a result from the ranking performance analysis, shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Targeting the top 20% of total mesh blocks represents a substantial reduction in the overall number of mesh blocks at 368/1,840 for Mornington Peninsula and 365/1,827 for Geelong.
source: Targeting of the top 20% of total mesh blocks for these two regions represents a substantial reduction in the overall number of mesh blocks at 368/1,840 and 365/1,827 for the Mornington Peninsula and Geelong models, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative calculation based on the model results.

claim: The geographical distribution of the top 20% of probability-ranked mesh blocks obtained with the excreta-informed models had obvious spatial clustering compared with the null models.
source: The geographical distribution of the top 20% of probability-ranked mesh blocks obtained with the excreta-informed models also had obvious spatial clustering compared with the null models (Figure 6A–D).
evidence: This is an observation from the spatial visualization of model predictions, shown in Figure 6.

claim: The non-random mesh block probability density of the excreta-informed models suggests these data can be used to inform rational, targeted, and cost-effective deployment of interventions.
source: The non-random mesh block probability density of the excreta-informed models (Figure 6B and D) suggests these data can be used to inform rational, targeted, and thus more cost-effective deployment of any interventions compared with reliance on human case data alone.
evidence: This is an inference about the practical application of the model results, based on Figure 6.

claim: Modeling based on the incubation period IQR provided better predictive capacity compared to using the absolute range of observed incubation periods.
source: However, this approach had an overall lower predictive capacity compared to the model based on the IQR of incubation periods (101–171 days). We observed a decrease in model AUC and the proportion of case-containing mesh blocks using the wider exposure period, indicating that the IQR is likely a more accurate estimation of the incubation period (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a result from the comparative analysis of different incubation period definitions.

claim: The long and variable incubation period of BU makes it difficult to establish when and where a person may have been infected with M. ulcerans, so the spatial information used by null models likely contains more 'noise' than excreta-informed models.
source: First, the long incubation period makes it difficult to establish both when and where a person may have been infected with M. ulcerans, so the spatial information used by the null models will likely contain more 'noise' than the excreta-informed models.
evidence: This is an inference about why the excreta-informed model performs better.

claim: Possums have a limited range, usually less than 100 m, so their excreta is a spatially trustworthy analyte.
source: Possums, however, have a limited range, usually less than 100 m, and so their excreta is a spatially trustworthy analyte, providing a more accurate picture of pathogen distribution in the environment (Fyfe et al., 2010; Buultjens et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by cited ecological studies of possum behavior.

claim: Human BU cases are not detected in areas where possums do not harbor M. ulcerans.
source: Second, human BU cases are not detected in areas where possums do not harbor M. ulcerans (Fyfe et al., 2010; Carson et al., 2014; Blasdell et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by cited field survey studies.

claim: Possums are playing a substantially more contributive role than humans to M. ulcerans transmission cycles.
source: Therefore, possums are playing a substantially more contributive role than humans to M. ulcerans transmission cycles, helping to explain why the excreta-informed model outperforms human BU case, incidence-based models.
evidence: This is an inference based on the epidemiological evidence and model performance.

claim: The ability of the excreta-informed model trained with Mornington Peninsula data to predict human case occurrence in Geelong strongly reinforces the link between possums harboring M. ulcerans and human BU cases across different geographic areas in southeast Australia.
source: The ability of the excreta-informed model trained with data from the Mornington Peninsula to predict human case occurrence in a distinct area (Geelong) strongly reinforces the link between possums harboring M. ulcerans and human BU cases across different geographic areas in southeast Australia.
evidence: This is an inference based on the successful prospective validation of the model.

claim: Targeted messaging based on predictive modeling may encourage preventative behaviors among local communities that could lessen the chances of transmission and reduce the number of emerging cases.
source: In addition, targeted messaging based on predictive modeling may also encourage preventative behaviors among local communities that could lessen the chances of transmission and reduce the number of emerging cases.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential public health applications.

claim: Targeted messaging promoting behaviors that mitigate known BU risk factors (e.g. mosquito bites) or promote known protective behaviors (use of insect repellent) could reduce disease incidence.
source: For example, targeted messaging promoting behaviors that mitigate known BU risk factors (e.g. mosquito bites) or promote known protective behaviors (use of insect repellent) could reduce disease incidence (Blasdell et al., 2022; Quek et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential interventions, supported by cited risk factor studies.

claim: Mosquitoes are likely vectors for M. ulcerans transmission between possums and humans.
source: In this study, we provide further evidence that BU in southeast Australia is a zoonotic infection involving Australian native possums in a transmission cycle. The means by which the pathogen is spread between possums and humans is under active investigation, but mosquitoes are likely vectors (Johnson et al., 2007; Lavender et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by cited research on potential transmission vectors.

claim: Possum excreta from Australian native possums in urban and semi-urban areas is highly abundant, easily recognized, and easily accessed.
source: Possum excreta fecal surveys are practical and cost-effective because excreta from Australian native possums in urban and semi-urban areas is highly abundant, easily recognized, and easily accessed.
evidence: This is based on the field experience and observations from the study.

claim: Roadside collection of possum excreta and subsequent molecular screening is relatively straightforward.
source: Roadside collection of possum excreta and subsequent molecular screening is also relatively straightforward and processing epizootiological data does not require informed consent or access to medical records.
evidence: This is based on the methodological experience from the study.

claim: Continuous excreta surveillance might detect trends in the distribution and epidemiology of BU in a region and allow assessment of the effectiveness of BU control measures.
source: Furthermore, as multiple years may elapse between the occurrences of BU in a particular region, continuous excreta surveillance might detect trends in the distribution and epidemiology of BU in a region and allow the effectiveness of any BU control measures; measures such as identifying and treating M. ulcerans-infected possum populations.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications of ongoing surveillance.

claim: Higher density sampling at 50 m intervals increased resolution for fecal mapping but didn't materially change the pattern of M. ulcerans positive fecal samples detected at 200 m sampling grids.
source: We explored the impact of sampling at a higher density (50 m intervals instead of 200 m) (Figure 3A). The higher density sampling provided by 50 m intervals increased resolution for the fecal mapping, but it didn't materially change the pattern of M. ulcerans positive fecal samples detected at 200 m sampling grids.
evidence: This is a result from the comparison of different sampling densities, shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 200 m sampling grids provide a pragmatic balance between survey sensitivity and survey time/costs.
source: We propose that 200 m sampling grids provide a pragmatic balance between survey sensitivity and survey time/costs.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the comparison of sampling densities.

claim: New field workers could be trained within a day using the streamlined workflow and custom-built tools.
source: The streamlined workflow, the custom-built distance trackers, and the use of Android mobile phones equipped with an electronic data collection solution simplified the fieldwork to such an extent that new field workers could be trained within a day.
evidence: This is based on the practical experience of implementing the survey methodology.

claim: ODK Collect proved a powerful tool for ensuring high-quality data collection as it automatically validated survey responses at the point of data collection.
source: Furthermore, ODK Collect proved a powerful tool for ensuring high-quality data collection as it only uploaded completed submissions, as the app automatically validated survey responses at the point of data collection by using entry constraints, error checks, and form logic.
evidence: This is based on the experience of using the ODK system for data collection.

claim: Using ODK significantly reduced data errors and data loss which would be much more common in paper surveys at this scale.
source: This significantly reduced data errors and data loss which would be much more common in paper surveys at this scale.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with traditional paper-based methods.

claim: The environmental surveillance system for BU using possum excreta will not directly translate to other BU endemic areas of the world, particularly West Africa, where there are no possums.
source: Finally, whilst this environmental surveillance system will assist BU control in southwest Australia, it will not directly translate to other BU endemic areas of the world, particularly the high-burden regions of West Africa, where there are no possums, and an equivalent animal reservoir is yet to be found.
evidence: This is a limitation of the approach based on the geographic specificity of the possum reservoir.

claim: An equivalent animal reservoir for M. ulcerans is yet to be found in West Africa.
source: Finally, whilst this environmental surveillance system will assist BU control in southwest Australia, it will not directly translate to other BU endemic areas of the world, particularly the high-burden regions of West Africa, where there are no possums, and an equivalent animal reservoir is yet to be found.
evidence: This reflects the current state of knowledge about BU reservoirs in Africa.
